title: Bengaluru Suburban Rail Project breaks ground at Yelahanka after a decade of delays
summary: The Bengaluru Suburban Rail Project began construction at Yelahanka station, ten years after it was first announced. Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah described the start as 'long overdue' and said it would 'transform mobility' for IT-corridor commutes. Residents along the route gave The Indian Express mixed reactions — some welcomed faster commutes, others worried about construction disruption and acquisition compensation.

key_claims.claim: Construction of the Bengaluru Suburban Rail Project began at Yelahanka station.
The project was first announced ten years ago.
The CM said the project would transform mobility for IT-corridor commuters.
Some residents welcomed faster commutes; others worried about construction noise and acquisition compensation.
The first phase covers 148 km of track across four corridors.
Total project budget stands at ₹15,767 crore.
